topic.title: Neural Verification and Constraint-Satisfying Architectures
topic.overview: Neural verification checks whether a network satisfies a property over an entire set of inputs, rather than only on tested examples. This topic includes robustness certificates, preimage bounds, differentiable optimization layers, and architectures that enforce constraints. A representative analysis shows limits of a broad convex-relaxation framework, separating solver quality from restrictions inherent in the relaxation.
topic.whyItMatters: Empirical success cannot establish that every allowed input respects a required bound. Verification and structural constraints provide stronger assurances, but their scope, approximation gaps, and computational costs must be made explicit.
topic.evolution: The representatives connect constrained optimization with input-convex networks and embedded optimization layers. Later work improves local Lipschitz certificates and verification domains. Recent architectures enforce input-dependent linear constraints directly, while related structured-network work considers how simplification affects implementable logic and accuracy.
openQuestions: Which architectural choices make useful properties easier to certify?
How can tighter guarantees scale without imposing unacceptable losses in prediction quality or inference speed?
